chunk_findings.detail: Given a valid but longer contact such as `export.security_contact = "https://example.com/report?token= [REDACTED] + "a" * 300`, `_reporting` calls `one_line(cfg.export.security_contact, 300)`, so the contact published in SECURITY.md is truncated to the 300-character limit rather than being the configured value. The knob accepts an arbitrarily long string and the config docs say the contact is written as given and exempt from redaction; silently cutting a reporting URL/email to 300 characters can make the published contact unusable and may also break any exact-value redaction exemption that relies on the configured text appearing unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_reporting

chunk_findings.detail: The new “exempt the contact” logic splits the whole rendered body on the configured `security_contact` string before redaction, so any other secret that contains that contact as a substring is broken into pieces that may no longer match the redactor’s patterns. For example, with `export.security_contact = "example.com"` and an export body containing the sensitive email `[REDACTED:email]`, line 44 splits the text into `"alice@"` and `""`. The redactor would normally redact the full email address, but after the split it only sees `"alice@"`, which is not a complete email pattern, so the local part is emitted unredacted. The intent was to exempt the reporting contact itself, not to disable redaction for unrelated secrets that merely contain the contact string.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/safe.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: The contact exemption is implemented by splitting the rendered text on the exact configured `security_contact` and redacting only the pieces between occurrences. That exempts the configured substring wherever it appears, including inside a larger token that should still be redacted. For example, if `export.security_contact = "[REDACTED:email]"` and the rendered body contains the different address `[REDACTED:email]`, `text.split(keep)` yields `["not", ""]`; neither piece contains a complete email address, so the redactor leaves both unchanged and the join returns `[REDACTED:email]` unredacted. The intended behavior is to leave only the configured contact visible while still redacting other email addresses, so this can leak redactable email addresses that contain the contact as a substring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/safe.py:redact_export_text

chunk_findings.detail: The new aggregation assumes `red.text(part).counts` is always a mapping, but the same file exposes `redaction_attrs(counts: Mapping[str, int] | None)` and documents a `redacted=off` header state. If the export redactor is disabled and the security body contains the configured contact, the redaction result used here can have `counts=None`, so the loop `for kind, n in part.counts.items()` raises `AttributeError` instead of returning the disabled-redaction result. Even if the disabled result uses an empty mapping rather than `None`, the code drops the original disabled/`None` state and reports ordinary zero redactions rather than `redacted=off`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/safe.py:redact_export_text

chunk_findings.detail: The new “stands alone” regex still does not treat `@` as a continuation of a longer address. Its negative lookahead is `(?!\.?[\w-])`, so after the contact an `@` is allowed and the contact is considered standing alone. With `export.security_contact = "alice"`, `safe.redact_text("write to [REDACTED:email]", cfg)` splits at `alice`, so `red.text` never sees the full `[REDACTED:email]` as one address; at minimum the local part `alice` remains in the output, and the email redaction count can be missed. This is the same redaction-bypass class as the earlier confirmed finding: the new probe only checks a domain contact inside a larger address and a full-address contact, not a configured contact that is an email local part.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/safe.py:_standing_alone

chunk_findings.detail: The rendering line collapses all whitespace with `" ".join(cfg.export.security_contact.split())`, but `safe.redact_text` still exempts only the raw configured value after `strip()`. If the operator sets a contact containing internal whitespace, e.g. `security_contact = "report  to  [REDACTED:email]"` or a TOML string with a newline inside the contact, the generated body contains the collapsed text while `safe`’s `keep` contains the uncollapsed text. Then `keep not in text` is true, the body is redacted as if no contact were configured, and the email inside the operator’s own reporting contact is replaced by `[REDACTED:email]` instead of being published.

chunk_findings.detail: The new normalization collapses whitespace only in the configured contact, not in the text being redacted. Given `cfg.export.security_contact = "mail  [REDACTED:email]\nor call the desk"` and a call such as `safe.redact_text("mail  [REDACTED:email]\nor call the desk", cfg)` (for example, a hand-edited reporting paragraph outside the generated region), `keep` becomes `"mail [REDACTED:email] or call the desk"`, which is not present in the text, so the function takes the `keep not in text` path and returns `red.text(text)`, redacting the published contact email. The previous `.strip()` behavior preserved the exact configured string and would have allowed this occurrence; the change introduces an over-redaction failure for any non-collapsed form of the contact.

data.summary: approval refusal from 'ddflow --repo <worktree> pins regenerate --approval request' tells the agent to run 'ddflow approvals ask <Q>', which answers 'no ask <Q>' unless --repo <worktree> is repeated: the hint omits the repo the request was filed under. Repro: cd /tmp; ddflow --repo WT pins regenerate --only readme-knobs --approval request, then ddflow approvals ask Q -> 'no ask Q', ddflow approvals pending -> none pending; with --repo WT both work.

data.body:
Fixes bug Bce739b2ffe: approval refusal from 'ddflow --repo <worktree> pins regenerate --approval request' tells the agent to run 'ddflow approvals ask <Q>', which answers 'no ask <Q>' unless --repo <worktree> is repeated: the hint omits the repo the request was filed under. Repro: cd /tmp; ddflow --repo WT pins regenerate --only readme-knobs --approval request, then ddflow approvals ask Q -> 'no ask Q', ddflow approvals pending -> none pending; with --repo WT both work. Found on SEC-policy-contact.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bce739b2ffe --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bce739b2ffe --regression-test <test>` first).
